prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-product of a sequence of letters is the product of the letter-values of its letters. When the square root of JULY's word-product is put into its simplest radical form of $a\sqrt{b}$, where $b$ has no perfect-square factors greater than 1, what is the value of $b$?

solutions.title: Prime factorize
solutions.body:
J = 10, U = 21, L = 12, Y = 25. Product $= 10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = (2 \cdot 5)(3 \cdot 7)(2^2 \cdot 3)(5^2) = 2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7$.
$\sqrt{2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7} = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\sqrt{2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7} = 30\sqrt{70}$, so $b = 70$.

**Answer: 70**

solutions.title: Compute the product
solutions.body:
$10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = 63{,}000 = 900 \times 70$, and $\sqrt{900} = 30$. 70 = $2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$ has no square factor, so $\sqrt{63000} = 30\sqrt{70}$ and $b = 70$.

**Answer: 70**

prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-product of a sequence of letters is the product of the letter-values of its letters. What sequence of letters has the same word-product as JULY, but (1) does not contain any of the letters in JULY, (2) contains the letter N, (3) does not contain any of its letters more than once and (4) has its letters in alphabetical order?

solutions.title: Use the prime factorization
solutions.body:
JULY's word-product is $2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7$. N = 14 $= 2 \cdot 7$, leaving $2^2 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3$.
Three factors of 5 must come from different letters whose values are multiples of 5, other than J (10) and Y (25): only E = 5, O = 15 and T = 20. Together they give $5 \cdot 15 \cdot 20 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5^3$, leaving a factor $3$: C = 3.
Letters C, E, N, O, T in alphabetical order: **CENOT**. (Adding A = 1 would not change the product; ACENOT is also accepted.)

**Answer: CENOT**

solutions.title: Check the product
solutions.body:
$C \cdot E \cdot N \cdot O \cdot T = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 14 \cdot 15 \cdot 20 = 63{,}000$ and $J \cdot U \cdot L \cdot Y = 10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = 63{,}000$ ✓. No letters repeat or come from JULY.

**Answer: CENOT**

prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-sum of a sequence of letters is the sum of the letter-values of its letters. The values of the letters of a particular four-letter sequence form an arithmetic sequence and this sequence has the same word-sum as JULY. What is the least possible value of a letter in this four-letter sequence?

solutions.title: Center at the average
solutions.body:
JULY's word-sum is $10 + 21 + 12 + 25 = 68$, average 17. A four-term arithmetic sequence is symmetric about its average: $17 - \frac{3d}{2}, 17 - \frac{d}{2}, 17 + \frac{d}{2}, 17 + \frac{3d}{2}$. For whole numbers $d$ must be even: $d = 2$: 14, 16, 18, 20; $d = 4$: 11, 15, 19, 23; $d = 6$: 8, 14, 20, 26; $d = 8$ would need 29 > 26. Least value: **8**.

**Answer: 8**

solutions.title: Equation
solutions.body:
$a + (a + d) + (a + 2d) + (a + 3d) = 4a + 6d = 68$, so $2a + 3d = 34$. To make $a$ small, make $d$ large, but $a + 3d \le 26$. $d = 6$: $a = 8$, largest term $26$ ✓; $d = 8$: $a = 5$, largest $29$ ✗. So the least value is 8.

**Answer: 8**
